name: Lemonade Stand
tagline: Classic summer stall — bottles, ice, a folding table.
locationHints: near your school gate after the last bell
the park corner on Sunday mornings
the street outside your building during the society mela
firstEventHints: The corner-shop aunty raises lemon prices two days before the school fair.
Your cousin Arjun asks for 10 chilled bottles for his cricket-match crowd.
A sudden afternoon shower empties the park — you still have 15 bottles iced.

name: Ice Cream Parlour
tagline: Cones, kulfi sticks, and a freezer borrowed from home.
locationHints: outside the school gate at 3 pm dismissal
the gully cricket ground on weekend evenings
your building's community hall during birthday bookings
firstEventHints: A power cut at 2 pm threatens to melt half your stock before the evening rush.
Priya's mom wants 40 kulfi sticks for her daughter's birthday on Saturday.
The ice-cream cart uncle two lanes away drops his price by ₹5 per scoop.

name: T-Shirt Shop
tagline: Plain tees, fabric paint, and your own cool designs.
locationHints: the school's annual-day stall where parents browse
the neighbourhood Diwali mela near the temple
your society's WhatsApp group for pre-orders
firstEventHints: Class 8B wants 25 matching tees for their farewell — but only if you can deliver in 5 days.
Your design supplier says blank tees are out of stock until next week.
Meera shows off the shirt she bought from you — three classmates message asking for the same one.

name: Game Studio
tagline: Tiny browser games you build with friends and share.
locationHints: your school's computer-club bulletin board
the society kids' WhatsApp group during holidays
the cousins' group chat after Eid get-togethers
firstEventHints: Rahul wants to join as co-designer, but he wants his name first in the credits.
A parent asks if you can make a simple maths game for her Class 5 son — she'll pay ₹200.
Your main game crashes on one friend's old phone — fixing it means delaying launch by a week.

name: Craft Shop
tagline: Handmade rakhis, diyas, bookmarks, and friendship bands.
locationHints: your society's Diwali stall with other kids
the school fundraiser near the auditorium
the Raksha Bandhan pop-up table outside the temple
firstEventHints: Neha's mom places a bulk order for 30 rakhis but wants a 20% discount.
You run out of silver beads three days before Diwali and the craft shop is 40 minutes away.
Your best-selling diya design is being copied by a stall two rows down.

name: School Blog
tagline: A blog about school life, homework hacks, and book reviews.
locationHints: shared in your class WhatsApp group each Friday
pinned on your school's student-council notice board
linked in your cousins' holiday group chat
firstEventHints: Your Class 7 exam-tips post suddenly gets 200 views in a day — strangers are asking for more.
Ananya offers to write one post a week, but she wants her name on the blog banner.
A local tuition centre messages asking to sponsor a post for ₹300 — it would be your first paid one.

name: My Business
tagline: Invent your own — something only you would think of.
locationHints: wherever your kind of customer actually hangs out
the place in your neighbourhood where people already buy things
a spot you know well — school, society, or the park nearby
firstEventHints: Describe your idea to Koko — what do you sell, and who's your very first customer?
Think of one thing you'd need to buy on day one — and one thing you'd try to borrow.
Picture Sanjay from your class seeing your stall for the first time — what pulls him in?
